All tests pass. 

## Summary

I added email uniqueness enforcement to `POST /api/owners`, rejecting duplicates with **409**, following the existing telephone-uniqueness pattern exactly.

New cohesive units (no existing method changed except the YAML wiring):

- **`CheckUniqueEmail`** — a new one-method function class. Reads the built `Owner` via `@Val`, and if it has an email, compares its lower-cased value against every other owner's, throwing `DuplicateEmailException` on a match.
- **`DuplicateEmailException`** — checked exception (extends `Exception`).
- **`DuplicateEmailHandler`** — escalation handler responding `409 CONFLICT`.
- **`DuplicateEmailException.yml`** — wires the exception to its handler.
- **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted a `checkEmail` step between `checkTelephone` and `checkHousehold`.

**Structural impact was kept minimal**: the only pre-existing function touched is the YAML pipeline (data, not code). All behaviour lives in brand-new small classes with `WMC_other = 0`, so no large class pays for the change. No existing Java method was modified.

Note: `Owner.setEmail` already lower-cases the stored value, but `CheckUniqueEmail` also lower-cases both sides defensively so the "lower-cased email" rule holds regardless of storage. Email is optional, so a null email short-circuits without a false conflict.

I added email uniqueness enforcement to `POST /api/owners`, rejecting duplicates with **409**, following the existing telephone-uniqueness pattern exactly.

New cohesive units (no existing method changed except the YAML wiring):

- **`CheckUniqueEmail`** — a new one-method function class. Reads the built `Owner` via `@Val`, and if it has an email, compares its lower-cased value against every other owner's, throwing `DuplicateEmailException` on a match.
- **`DuplicateEmailException`** — checked exception (extends `Exception`).
- **`DuplicateEmailHandler`** — escalation handler responding `409 CONFLICT`.
- **`DuplicateEmailException.yml`** — wires the exception to its handler.
- **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted a `checkEmail` step between `checkTelephone` and `checkHousehold`.

**Structural impact was kept minimal**: the only pre-existing function touched is the YAML pipeline (data, not code). All behaviour lives in brand-new small classes with `WMC_other = 0`, so no large class pays for the change. No existing Java method was modified.

Note: `Owner.setEmail` already lower-cases the stored value, but `CheckUniqueEmail` also lower-cases both sides defensively so the "lower-cased email" rule holds regardless of storage. Email is optional, so a null email short-circuits without a false conflict.
